what_this_is: Every file the estate's committed tree publishes under /interop/, with its size, its sha256 and how it is served. Built by reading the tree, so it is a measurement, not a list of intentions. Three served states occur, because there are three — a path routed to the mirror is not the same path as one the estate serves from its retired-bytes archive, and a fourth state (retired-bytes-absent) is reserved for a retired record the archive does not hold, which is not emitted because the archive is a deploy-time artefact and naming its membership here would make this index stale on every deploy.
how_to_verify: sha256 is the digest of the file's bytes as published. Fetch the path and hash it; on a row whose served_bytes reads 'as-published', a match means you hold what the estate published. Three things to know when it does not match: the digest is of the bytes at THIS index's source_commit, and the live site serves the bytes of the currently DEPLOYED commit, so the two agree once that commit is deployed; for pages-served HTML the digest is over the BUILT file, which carries the workspace-launcher script the build injects; and the EDGE rewrites some HTML in transit, so on a row whose served_bytes reads 'edge-transformed' or 'edge-transformed-per-request' the bytes the site serves are NOT the bytes published here, and on a 'per-request' row they differ on every fetch, so no digest of them can be reproduced by anyone, including us. A row whose served state is hf-mirror is a different case again: the bytes come from the HuggingFace evidence mirror, which is a SEPARATE HOST whose membership this index does not record, so the row's digest is checkable only while the mirror still holds the file. For retired-bytes paths the digest is of the canonical bytes, which the archive copies verbatim.
retired: A retired record is HISTORICAL evidence of a past measurement, never current proof. The estate's server marks these with the response header x-evidence-state: retired-or-invalid-historical-bytes. BEING RETIRED IS NOT THE SAME AS BEING UNREACHABLE: a retired path that is served answers 200 and its bytes verify against the sha256 below; a retired path that is not served answers 404. The `served` field says which.

served_legend.hf-mirror: routed by a 302 redirect to the HuggingFace evidence mirror (scripts/deploy-exclusions.json); the sha256 is of the canonical tree bytes, which are the bytes the mirror holds. THE MIRROR IS A SEPARATE HOST AND ITS MEMBERSHIP IS NOT RECORDED HERE, so this row's claim is true UNDER THE CONDITION THAT THE MIRROR STILL HOLDS THE FILE. MEASURED 2026-11-07: all five mirror classes (mill-cards-signed, mill-cards-unsigned, mill-evidence, the file-kind exclusions and the ots/*.invalid records) resolved ANONYMOUSLY with HTTP 200 and an exact digest match. If the mirror ever stops holding a path, the reader gets HUGGINGFACE's 'Entry not found' — a 404 and a 15-byte body from the mirror, NOT from this site — so a mismatch on one of these rows is a statement about the mirror's membership until it is shown otherwise
served_legend.retired-bytes: a retired .invalid record. The estate's Function intercepts every .invalid path and serves it from the retired-bytes archive when that archive holds these exact bytes (200, x-evidence-state: retired-or-invalid-historical-bytes), and answers 404 BY DESIGN when it does not. The sha256 is of the canonical tree bytes, which are the bytes the archive copies verbatim. Which case applies is decided by the archive in force, published at /archive/retired-proof-bytes-v1.json
served_legend.retired-bytes-absent: reserved for the membership-specific variant; not emitted, because the archive is a deploy-time artefact and naming it here would make the index stale on every deploy

served_bytes_legend.as-published: the bytes the site serves for this path are the bytes the estate published here; the sha256 is checkable against a fetch
served_bytes_legend.edge-transformed: the edge rewrites this markup in transit, so the bytes the site serves are NOT the bytes published here; the sha256 is of the published bytes and will not match a fetch
served_bytes_legend.edge-transformed-per-request: the edge rewrites this markup and the rewrite is randomised per request, so the bytes the site serves differ on EVERY fetch; no digest of them can be reproduced, by a reader or by the estate
